title: Interactive parameter diagnostics and guided repair flow for tool/function calls
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem statement: Engineers integrating tool/function calling see opaque JSON validation errors from the runtime that are hard to triage (e.g., generic 'invalid params' or long schema dumps). This causes slower integration, repeated support tickets, and risky workaround patterns (silent coercion in clients). Goal: ship an interactive diagnostics flow that produces concise, actionable error messages with suggested repairs, a reproducible minimal example, and optional auto-fix recommendations for SDKs and the Console. Scope: - Schema-aware error classification (type mismatch, missing required, enum mismatch, extra properties, format violation) - Human-friendly messages with one-line summary + prioritized suggestions - Structured diagnostic payloads the Console and SDKs can consume to present guided UI helpers - Optional single-click auto-fix for safe repairs (e.g., string->number coercion when unambiguous) - Developer CLI command that reproduces the failing call and prints diffs - Backwards-compat: we must not change existing schema registry format; diagnostics consumed via new metadata envelope

Out of scope: full automatic repair for ambiguous semantic errors (e.g., wrong domain entity), telemetry dashboards (follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime emits a 'diagnostic' metadata object alongside validation failure responses containing: succinct error_code, human_message, suggestions (ranked), reproducible_example_snippet, and confidence_score; 2) Console surfaces the message with a 'Show suggested fixes' drawer and an 'Apply safe fix' button for deterministic coercions; 3) SDKs (python/js) expose a developer-cli 'redwood diag reproduce' that runs the failing example locally and prints a colorized diff; 4) Unit + integration tests covering type mismatch, missing required, enums, extra props, and format errors; 5) Migration guidance documented in Confluence and linked in the API error page.
milestones: Runtime implementation: error classification module (in progress)
SDK integration: diagnostic envelope parser + CLI (next)
Console UI: drawer and safe-fix flow (queued)
updates: 2026-02-23: Kickoff meeting. Attendees: Amina, Luca, Priya (Console), Mateo (SDKs). Agreed to keep schema registry unchanged and add a 'diagnostic' envelope for failures. Action: Amina to write RFC.

2026-02-28: RFC posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TOOL/Interactive+Parameter+Diagnostics. Key trade-offs: verbose schema dumps are useful for debuggers but terrible in UX; we will keep a verbose blob in diagnostics only and default to concise messages in API responses.

2026-03-04: Prototype classifier submitted (ENG-821999-proto) that maps ajv-style validation failures to our taxonomy. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1532. Early results: correctly classifies missing required and type mismatch in ~98% of fuzz tests; enum mismatch edgecases still noisy.

2026-03-08: Design review with Console team. Decided on three-tier suggestion ranking: safe (auto-fixable), recommended (manual copy/paste), risky (explain semantics). Console will only enable 'Apply safe fix' for safe suggestions and will show a warning for recommended ones.

2026-03-12: SDK spec landed for diagnostic envelope (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/pull/882). CLI prototype 'rw-diag reproduce' implemented in python-sdk. Next: add deterministic coercion rules and integrate into dev CLI tests.
implementation_notes: Runtime: add validator wrapper that returns DiagnosticEnvelope on validation failure. Schema parsing should capture: field_path, expected_shape_short, received_example, suggestion_hints (max 3), and helpful_link. Example error codes: DIAG_MISSING_REQUIRED, DIAG_TYPE_MISMATCH, DIAG_ENUM_MISMATCH, DIAG_EXTRA_PROPERTY, DIAG_FORMAT_INVALID. SDKs: map envelope to user-facing classes with to_console_button() and cli_apply_fix(). For safe coercions: implement deterministic rules only: string->number when string matches /^\s*-?\d+(\.\d+)?\s*$/; number->string when requested; boolean coercion only when literal strings 'true'/'false'. Ensure telemetry flags are opt-in and PII is redacted (no raw user text sent).
testing_plan: Unit tests for classifier mapping (100% coverage for known validator error shapes). Integration tests that assert SDK CLI reproduces failing request and that Console shows 'Apply safe fix' button only for safe cases. Fuzz tests against random schema/values to ensure no unsafe auto-fix is suggested. Privacy tests that verify no user PII is present in telemetry payloads. Canary rollout to 10% of hosted API keys for 2 weeks with monitoring on 'apply fix' acceptance rate and support ticket delta.
rollout_and_migration: Phase 1 (canary): enable diagnostic envelope in responses for 10% of traffic (internal + opt-in customers). Phase 2: SDKs ship CLI + opt-in auto-fix flags. Phase 3: Console safe-fix UI enabled for customers on dev/alpha clusters. Provide migration docs and best-practices: how to parse envelope, how to log diagnostics without noisy schema dumps, and how to opt out of telemetry.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect auto-fix could change semantics (e.g., coerced id types). Mitigation: only implement narrow deterministic rules and expose 'preview' before applying. Risk: exposing user data in diagnostics. Mitigation: redaction layer and strict PII scrubbing for telemetry. Risk: spec drift across SDKs. Mitigation: single source of truth in runtime schema helper and a cross-repo integration test that validates envelopes remain stable.
notes_for_reviewers: Please review deterministic coercion rules and the proposed error_code set. Security to review redaction rules. Console to confirm UX prototypes are feasible with the suggested drawer layout. SDKs to validate CLI UX. Schedule a 1-hour sync with stakeholders after initial feedback.
